subject: ela
intro: Digital tools are technology tools like computers, tablets, and keyboards that help us write, publish, and share our writing. In Grade 1, students learn to use a keyboard to type words, understand how a screen shows typed letters, and think about how digital writing can be shared with others. Digital writing and handwriting are both ways to communicate, and each has its own strengths.

items.prompt: What is a keyboard? What do you use it for?

steps: A keyboard is a tool with letter, number, and symbol keys.
When you press a key, that letter or symbol appears on the screen.
We use a keyboard to type words, sentences, and stories on a computer or tablet.
The keyboard is one of the most important digital writing tools.
solution.answer: A keyboard is a tool with keys for letters and numbers. You press the keys to type words on a screen.

items.prompt: How is typing on a keyboard different from writing with a pencil?

steps: When you write with a pencil, you form each letter by hand on paper.
When you type on a keyboard, you press a key and the letter appears on the screen automatically.
Typing can be faster once you learn where the keys are.
Pencil writing is easy to do anywhere, even without electricity.
Typed writing is easy to fix by deleting and retyping.
solution.answer: With a pencil you form letters by hand on paper. With a keyboard you press keys and letters appear on a screen. Typed writing is easy to change; handwriting requires erasing.

items.prompt: A student wrote a story on paper. Her teacher says she can type it and share it online with her classmates. Why might sharing digitally be helpful?

steps: When a story is on paper, only people who hold that paper can read it.
When a story is typed and shared digitally, many people can read it at the same time.
You can share it by email or through a class website without printing copies.
This means more people can enjoy your writing.
solution.answer: Sharing digitally allows many classmates to read the story at the same time without needing a paper copy.

items.prompt: What does the 'delete' or 'backspace' key do? How is it helpful when typing?

steps: The delete or backspace key removes the last letter or word you typed.
This is helpful when you make a mistake while typing.
Instead of crossing out or erasing, you just press the key.
This makes it easy to fix errors without starting over.
solution.answer: The delete key removes letters you typed. It is helpful because you can fix mistakes quickly without crossing out.

items.prompt: A student wants to publish her poem for the whole school to read. Should she hand out 100 paper copies or post it on the school website? What are the benefits of the digital option?

steps: Posting on the school website means anyone with a device can read it.
No paper is needed, so it is less wasteful.
It can be shared instantly without copying or printing.
Many people — students, teachers, parents — can all read it at the same time.
The digital option is faster, wider reaching, and uses no paper.
solution.answer: Posting on the school website allows everyone to read it instantly without printing. It is faster, saves paper, and reaches more readers.

items.prompt: A student is typing her name on a keyboard. She types 'Emly' by mistake. What key should she press to fix it before typing the missing letter?
items.hint: Think about which key removes the last letter typed.

steps: She should press the backspace or delete key.
That will remove the 'y.'
Then she types 'i' and 'y' to correct it to 'Emily.'
solution.answer: She should press the backspace key to delete 'y,' then type 'i' and then 'y' to spell 'Emily' correctly.

items.prompt: Name TWO digital tools that a Grade 1 student could use to write a story.
items.hint: Think about devices with screens and keyboards.

steps: A computer with a keyboard is one digital writing tool.
A tablet with a touch keyboard is another.
Both allow you to type and save writing.
solution.answer: Two digital tools: a computer with a keyboard and a tablet with a touch keyboard.

items.prompt: Give one advantage of writing on paper and one advantage of writing on a computer.
items.hint: Think about when you might NOT have electricity, and when you want to share something widely.

steps: Paper advantage: you can write anywhere — no electricity needed.
Computer advantage: you can share your writing with many people instantly and fix errors easily.
solution.answer: Paper advantage: you can write anywhere without electricity. Computer advantage: you can easily fix mistakes and share with many readers at once.

items.prompt: How could a class use a digital tool to publish a class book that all families could read at home?
items.hint: Think about how a file can be shared electronically.

steps: Each student types their page on a computer.
The teacher combines all the pages into one digital document.
The teacher emails it or posts it on the class website.
Families can open it on any device and read the class book at home.
solution.answer: Students type their pages, the teacher combines them into a digital document, and families can read it on any device after receiving it by email or class website.

items.prompt: What does 'publish' mean in writing? How is publishing digitally different from publishing on paper?
items.hint: Publishing means making your writing available for others to read.

steps: Publishing means sharing your finished writing with an audience.
Publishing on paper means printing and handing out copies.
Publishing digitally means posting it on a website, sending by email, or uploading to a shared folder.
Digital publishing can reach many more readers instantly and without printing costs.
solution.answer: Publishing means sharing your writing with readers. Publishing digitally shares it online with many people at once. Publishing on paper means printing copies.
